p: Corby stood on a rock and gave absolution — all nearby troops of any faith knelt or bowed their heads.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (chronology commentary)
p.short: Site chronology commentary on “Father Corby's absolution.”, Day 2

p: Cross killed entering the Wheatfield. Zook mortally wounded. Brooke's brigade pushes farthest into the Wheatfield of any Union brigade. Semmes's Confederates mortally wounded.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Cross killed entering the Wheatfield.”, Day 2

p: Wofford's fresh Georgia brigade sweeps through the Wheatfield behind the retreating Caldwell — reaches the farthest Confederate penetration toward Cemetery Ridge. Tilton's controversial withdrawal exposed the Union flank.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Wofford's fresh Georgia brigade sweeps through the Wheatfield behind the retreating Caldwell…”, Day 2

p: Crawford's Pennsylvania Reserves charge down the western slope of Little Round Top — drives Wofford's exhausted Confederates back through the Wheatfield. Colonel Taylor of 13th PA Reserves killed. Caldwell's position partially restored.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Crawford's Pennsylvania Reserves charge down the western slope of Little Round Top — drives…”, Day 2

p: SICKLES WOUNDED. Artillery shell shatters Sickles's right leg near the Trostle Farm. Sickles famously smokes a cigar as he is carried from the field. Birney assumes III Corps command.

McGilvery's emergency artillery line. McGilvery assembles guns from multiple batteries — Bigelow, Phillips, Hart — along Plum Run to plug the gap left by III Corps collapse. Bigelow's battery ordered to hold without support.

p.short: Site chronology entry “McGilvery's emergency artillery line.”, Day 2

p: BIGELOW'S TROSTLE FARM WITHDRAWAL. Bigelow's 9th Massachusetts battery ordered to hold as long as possible to buy time for McGilvery. Battery fights by prolonge (rope), losing guns one by one. Heroic withdrawal saves McGilvery's line.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Bigelow's Trostle Farm Withdrawal”, Day 2

p: 1ST MINNESOTA'S CHARGE. Cemetery Ridge gap is open. Wilcox's Confederate brigade advancing toward the gap. Hancock has nothing to send but Colvill's 262-man 1st Minnesota. 'My God, are these all the men we have?' Orders them to charge Wilcox's entire brigade to buy 5 minutes.

p.short: Site chronology entry “1ST MINNESOTA'S CHARGE.”, Day 2

p: 1st Minnesota engages Wilcox's Confederate brigade. Both flanks overlapped but the charge stops Wilcox long enough for reinforcements to arrive. Colvill wounded, Messick killed, Coates assumes command. 85.5% casualties.

p.short: Site chronology entry “1st Minnesota engages Wilcox's Confederate brigade.”, Day 2

p: Wilcox's advance halted. Reinforcements close the gap on Cemetery Ridge. Wright's Georgia brigade briefly breaks through Cemetery Ridge north of Wilcox but is driven back without support.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Wilcox's advance halted.”, Day 2

p: Stuart arrives with his cavalry after controversial absence. Lee reportedly greets him: 'General Stuart, where have you been?' Confederate cavalry now available for the first time since before the campaign began.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Stuart arrives with his cavalry after controversial absence.”, Day 2

p: Johnson's Confederate division advances on Culp's Hill at dusk. XII Corps has been stripped away to reinforce Cemetery Ridge leaving only Greene's brigade (1,424 men) to hold the entire hill against 6,500 Confederates.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Johnson's Confederate division advances on Culp's Hill at dusk.”, Day 2

p: Greene's lone stand is one of the finest defensive performances of the war — 1,424 men holding against 6,500.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (chronology commentary)
p.short: Site chronology commentary on “Johnson's Confederate division advances on Culp's Hill at dusk.”, Day 2

p: GREENE'S LONE STAND. Greene's brigade holds Culp's Hill alone. Johnson's Confederates (Stonewall Brigade, Jones, Nicholls, Steuart) assault repeatedly. Greene extends his thin line and bends but never breaks.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Greene's Lone Stand”, Day 2

p: Steuart's Confederate brigade occupies vacant XII Corps breastworks on lower Culp's Hill — the right of the Union position. XII Corps (returning from Cemetery Ridge) finds their own works occupied by Confederates.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Steuart's Confederate brigade occupies vacant XII Corps breastworks on lower Culp's Hill —…”, Day 2

p: XII Corps returns to Culp's Hill and finds Confederate troops in their works. Night attack repossesses most of the upper works. Lower works remain Confederate. Sets up the July 3 morning fight.

p.short: Site chronology entry “XII Corps returns to Culp's Hill and finds Confederate troops in their works.”, Day 2
